\begin{lemma}[Entries in flattened blocks]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.getD_flatten_block}
\label{Complexity.Codec.getD_flatten_block}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.take_drop_flatten}
\difficulty{3}
Let $L$ be a finite list of finite lists of elements of a type, and let $w$ be a natural
number such that every list in $L$ has length $w$. For natural numbers $j,t$ with $j$
less than the number of lists in $L$ and $t<w$, and any element $d$, the entry of the
concatenation of the lists at position $wj+t$ is equal to the entry of the $j$th list at
position $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Configuration word contains its cell chunks]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.getD_cfgWord_chunk}
\label{Complexity.Codec.getD_cfgWord_chunk}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.cellOf, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord, Complexity.Codec.chunkBit, Complexity.Codec.chunksWord, Complexity.Codec.getD_encChunk, Complexity.Codec.getD_flatten_block, Complexity.Codec.length_chunksWord, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a
Boolean input word, let $s\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $C$ be a configuration on input $x$.
For every chunk index $j<2s+1$ and bit index $t<W(N)$, the bit of the configuration word
at position $W(N)j+t$ equals bit $t$ of the encoding of the cell at index $j$ relative
to shift $s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Initial configuration check]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.InitChk}
\label{Complexity.Codec.InitChk}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.ValidChk, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.hH, Complexity.Codec.vScan, Complexity.Codec.wP, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$
be a Boolean string, and let $s$ be a natural number. The word $w$ passes the validity
check for input length $|x|$ and space parameter $s$; scanning its initial segment of
length $W(N)(2s+1)$ yields initial state $q_0$ with head position $0$ and the indicated
Boolean flag true; the bit value of the following segment of length $w_P(|x|)$ is $1$;
and either $N$ has no work tapes or the specified bit of $w$ is true.
\end{definition}

Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$ be a
Boolean input, let $s$ be a natural number, and let $w$ be a Boolean list. The predicate
holds exactly when $w$ is a valid check for input length $|x|$ and time parameter $s$,
and scanning the prefix of $w$ of length $W(N)(2s+1)$ yields the terminal scan result
$(	ext{none},1)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Head-position update]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.movePos}
\label{Complexity.Codec.movePos}
\leanok
Let $n$ and $p$ be natural numbers. For a head movement that stays in place, the updated
position is $p$; for a rightward movement, it is $p$ when $p=n+1$ and otherwise $p+1$;
for a leftward movement, it is the natural-number subtraction $p-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Value of the Moved Input Head]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.val_moveInputPos}
\label{Complexity.Codec.val_moveInputPos}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.movePos, Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $p$ be a head position among $0,\ldots,n+1$, and let
$mv\in\{-1,0,1\}$. The value of the clamped input-head movement is $p$ when $mv=0$, is
$p+1$ when $mv=1$ and $p\ne n+1$, and is $p$ when $mv=1$ and $p=n+1$; when $mv=-1$, it
is $\max(p-1,0)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Input symbol at a position]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.inpOf}
\label{Complexity.Codec.inpOf}
\leanok
Let $x$ be a Boolean list and $p$ a natural-number position. The input symbol at $p$ is
absent when $p=0$ or $p=|x|+1$; otherwise it is the symbol of $x$ at index $p-1$, using
false when that index is out of range.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Input symbol via the position function]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.inputSymbol_eq}
\label{Complexity.Codec.inputSymbol_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.inpOf, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$
be a Boolean input word, and let $C$ be a configuration on $x$. The symbol read by the
input head equals the following option-valued function of its position $p$: it is absent
when $p=0$ or $p=|x|+1$, and otherwise it is the Boolean symbol at index $p-1$,
defaulting to false if that index is out of range.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Encoded computation step check]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.StepChk}
\label{Complexity.Codec.StepChk}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Gs, Complexity.Codec.ValidChk, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.aI, Complexity.Codec.inpOf, Complexity.Codec.movePos, Complexity.Codec.sDone, Complexity.Codec.sScan, Complexity.Codec.vScan, Complexity.Codec.wP, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet; let $x$ be a
Boolean input, $s$ a natural number, and $w,w'$ Boolean lists. The predicate requires
that $w$ is a valid check for input length $|x|$ and parameter $s$, that
$|w'|=W(N)(2s+1)+w_P(|x|)+1$, and that the entry of $w'$ at index $W(N)(2s+1)+w_P(|x|)$
is true. It also requires a Boolean choice $b$ such that the encoded input-head position
in the indicated segment of $w'$ equals the position obtained by moving the position
encoded in the corresponding segment of $w$ according to the input-head movement
determined from the scan of $w$, the input symbol at that position, and $b$; finally,
the indicated scan of the two transition results on the prefixes of $w$ and $w'$ must
report true completion.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Splitting a bit string at a marked final bit]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.word_split}
\label{Complexity.Codec.word_split}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $w$ be a finite bit string and let $a,b$ be natural numbers. If $|w|=a+b+1$ and the
bit of $w$ at index $a+b$ is $1$, then $w$ is the concatenation of its first $a$ bits,
the next $b$ bits, and the one-bit string $1$.
\end{lemma}

\lean{Complexity.Codec.sScan_sel}

\uses{Complexity.Codec.SX, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.blocksD, Complexity.Codec.sInit, Complexity.Codec.sScan, Complexity.Codec.sScan_eq, Complexity.Codec.slStep}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $G$ be a
family of local update rules indexed by a Boolean, and let $u,u'$ be Boolean words whose
lengths are both $W_Nm$ for some natural number $m$. For either Boolean $b$, the
component of the paired scan corresponding to $b$ equals the fold of the update rule
$G(b)$ over the paired decoded length-$W_N$ blocks, starting from the initial scan
state.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of valid configuration codes]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.validLang_iff}
\label{Complexity.Codec.validLang_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.ValidChk, Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_eq_bits_iff, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.Codec.validChk_iff, Complexity.Codec.validLang, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and work-tape
symbols, let $x,w$ be finite bit strings, and let $s$ be a natural number. Encode a pair
of bit strings by doubling every bit of the first string, appending the separator $01$,
and then appending the second string. The encoding of $x$ paired with the encoding of
$w$ and the binary expansion of $s$ belongs to the language of codes for configurations
of $N$ whose work-tape heads and nonblank cells lie within distance $s$ of the origin if
and only if the following conditions hold: $w$ has length $W_N(2s+1)+P(|x|)+1$, where
$W_N$ is the fixed cell-code width determined by $N$ and $P(n)$ is the length of the
binary expansion of $n+1$; scanning the first $W_N(2s+1)$ bits yields an accepting scan
state; the value of the next $P(|x|)$ bits, interpreted as a binary expansion, is at
most $|x|+1$; and the final bit is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Accepted language check characterization]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang_iff}
\label{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.AcceptChk, Complexity.Codec.acceptChk_iff, Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_eq_bits_iff, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and let $x,w$
be finite bit strings and $s$ a natural number. The paired encoding of $x$ with the
paired encoding of $w$ and the binary expansion of $s$ belongs to the language of
accepting configuration codes for $N$ if and only if $w$ passes the following check: its
length is $W(N)(2s+1)+w_P(|x|)+1$; scanning its first $W(N)(2s+1)$ bits yields an
accepting validator state and the head/output summary $(	ext{halted},1)$; the binary
value of the next $w_P(|x|)$ bits is at most $|x|+1$; and the final bit is $1$. Here
$W(N)$ is the encoded width of one cell block and $w_P(n)$ is the bit width used for an
input-head position when the input length is $n$.
\end{theorem}
